title: Model entry stepper + pin copy experiments (WIP)
content:
Context:
This is a working doc for a linear stepper to create an endpoint from the model catalog + the microcopy we show around model version pinning and fallback behavior. Goal is to reduce confusion around: what pinning does, when it is appropriate, and how automatic fallbacks behave under Dedicated/Private deployments.

Audience:
- Product + PMs (console)
- Eng: frontend + backend owners for endpoint creation APIs
- UX writers and solutions engineering for copy alignment

High level constraint: keep fast-path creation (3 clicks) for most self-serve use cases, but surface advanced pinning controls in the same flow without modal overload. The stepper below is intentionally minimal with an expandable section for advanced routing/pinning.

Wireframe summary (linear stepper):
1) Step 1: Choose model
   - Catalog grid (cards) + inline filters: task, cost tier, latency profile, region
   - Quick-compare toast: up to 3 models selected to compare metrics (p50/p95 latency, token cost estimate per 1k tokens, compatible runtimes)
   - Microcopy draft (card footer): "Default variant will route to latest validated revision for best throughput. Click 'Pin' to lock a specific revision."

2) Step 2: Endpoint basics (name, route, region)
   - Name (free text) + generated slugs auto-filled (editable)
   - Route scope dropdown: global | region-scoped | private (VPC)
   - Dropdown help text: "Selecting 'region-scoped' pins traffic to chosen region and affects routing/fallbacks."

3) Step 3: Capacity & SLA
   - Preset buttons: bursty dev | small prod | large prod (maps to Dedicated capacity configs)
   - Cost estimate panel: shows monthly estimated spend for chosen preset and expected throughput

4) Step 4: Pinning & fallback (collapsed by default)
   - Toggle: "Pin model version (advanced)"
   - When toggled open: list of available revisions with metadata (commit, date, validation status, notes) and default suggestion (latest validated)
   - Microcopy drafts: 
       * Title: "Pin a model revision"
       * Primary help: "Pinning locks the endpoint to the selected model revision. This prevents automatic rollouts when we add new revisions to the model."
       * Secondary: "If the pinned revision is unavailable, you can configure fallbacks below (recommended for production)."
   - Fallback controls (radio): No fallback | Auto-fallback to latest validated | Fallback to specific alternate revision
   - Small bold warning line (if user picks No fallback): "No fallback will cause requests to fail if the pinned revision becomes unreachable. Use only when you manage your own uptime guarantees."

Copy experiments (variants):
- Variant A (explicit):
  "Pinning locks this endpoint to a specific model revision. You will not receive updates from newer revisions unless you unpin or create a new endpoint. If the pinned revision is offline, requests will fail without a fallback."

- Variant B (actionable + short):
  "Lock to revision (recommended for stable production). Can opt into an automatic fallback if the locked revision is unavailable."

- Variant C (risk-focused):
  "Pin revision — prevents unexpected changes to outputs. If pinned revision becomes unavailable, traffic stops; enable fallback to keep serving."

Hypotheses to validate:
- H1: Users prefer a short, one-line explanation (Variant B) when first encountering the toggle; detailed explanation can live in an expandable help row.
- H2: Providing an explicit fallback choice in the creation flow reduces support tickets about endpoints going down after a model upload.
- H3: Showing a small cost delta when choosing fallback (if fallback points to higher-cost runtime) reduces accidental high-cost fallback selections.

Open questions / backlog notes:
- Q1: When customers are on Dedicated with multi-variant routing (e.g., cost-tier fallback), how do we surface the effective cost estimate? (ENG-2345)
- Q2: Should we allow pinning to a model variant (quantized vs full) in addition to revision? Feels useful for Private deployments that use quantized runtime.
- Q3: How to represent cross-region fallback latency/RESIDENCY implications (legal/data residency) in the UI copy?

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Stepper implemented with steps 1-4 and collapsed Pinning panel
- Toggle persists to backend create endpoint payload (pin: {revision_id, fallback_policy})
- Validation errors surfaced inline for: missing name, invalid route, pinning a revision not available in selected region
- Tooltips and help copy for the three microcopy variants included for A/B testing

Telemetry & metrics to capture during test:
- % of users who expand pinning panel during creation
- % of endpoints created with pin enabled vs not
- % of pin-enabled endpoints that also configure a fallback
- Support ticket rate for "endpoint offline after model upload" before vs after roll out

Edge cases called out for engineering:
- Backend should return compatible revisions per region/runtime. UI must not show pin options that the backend cannot guarantee.
- When creating an endpoint from a versioned model that has ongoing validation jobs, show status tag (validating) and block pining to unvalidated revisions (or show warn and require explicit confirmation).

Copy library (short strings for UI elements):
- Pin toggle label: "Pin model version"
- Pin help short: "Lock endpoint to a specific revision"
- Fallback label options: "No fallback", "Auto: latest validated", "Fallback: choose revision"
- Warning: "Requests will fail if pinned revision is unreachable"
- CTA create: "Create endpoint" / secondary "Save draft"

Prototype notes and next steps:
- Frontend: wireframe assets in /prototypes/stepper-pin (see linked PR) need responsive states for mobile narrow widths (collapse pin panel earlier).
- UX writer: pick one variant for first experiment (recommend Variant B) and craft the expandable help with examples (e.g., ML team scenario).
- Eng: backend ticket to accept pin payload and persist fallback policy: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-2345
- Release plan: behind feature flag for early enterprise beta; gather telemetry for 4 weeks then iterate.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- Focus feedback on the tone of the primary microcopy and the wording of the No fallback warning. Looking to be concise but clear about operational risk.
- If you think we should surface pinning earlier (card level in catalog) call that out — tradeoff is noise vs discoverability.

Hand-off checklist (when ready for dev):
- Final copy decided and staged in /docs/ui-copy-endpoint-pins.md
- Figma frames: baseline + expanded pin panel + validation states
- API contract: POST /endpoints accepts: model_id, revision_id (nullable), fallback_policy enum
- E2E test plan for: create pinned endpoint, pinned revision gone offline, verify fallback behavior

----

Random scribbles / quick ideas (freeform):
- Tiny badge on catalog card: "Stable (pinnable)" vs "Rolling"
- Add a one-click "Pin latest validated" button on a previously created endpoint details page (for ops).
- Consider an audit log entry with the pin/unpin event for compliance (Private customers will want this).

End of WIP.
